notes: Fifth sweep (previous sweep at 3e3581d): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, each result.json recording head ba24972 with no uncommitted changes and skill_hash 1fd3c153..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder; every transcript contains the new Formatting bullet ("formatting is part of writing a file"). Opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md only; haiku-2 also read references/library-design.md, an extra read as in earlier sweeps, so Expected reads is met in all five. Each session wrote orders.ex once and ran mix format --check-formatted on it. In the scratch folder all five pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with --warnings-as-errors against a stand-in Decimal written there (the Hex cache still has no decimal package), with no warning, and each has one doctest block on build/1 that passes against the stand-in. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day in all five), top customers with zero-count customers left out in all five, and empty results for []. All five return {:error, reason} for a bad amount, an unknown status, a missing key and a bad date. Haiku-1 reports last_placed_at as a DateTime where the prompt asks for a date, and haiku-2 returns customers as a sorted list of summaries rather than a map; no rule covers either, so they are noted in the summaries only. The sessions' own check scripts (opus-1 test.exs, haiku-1 decimal_stub.ex, haiku-2 stub_decimal.exs and check_test.exs) sit in their session scratchpads and are not graded.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 372). The sentences "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line. When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks." are replaced by "A function may mix the forms: a short clause on `do:`, a clause that needs a block as a block, each block clause set apart with a blank line." That sentence decides no verdict here: no function in the five files mixes do: and block clauses (the previous sweep's one mixed function, haiku-2's parse_orders/2, is now a reduce_while in every run). Violating runs out of 5, per sentence: do: on a body of several steps 0; a case, with or comment under do: 0; a mixed function whose block clause is not set apart 0 (none exercised); a do: body wrapped onto a line of its own, on a function or an if, 0: every do: sits on its head's line, at opus-1 lines 192-193 and 220-223, haiku-1 127-130 and 170, haiku-2 114-117, sonnet-1 137-140 and sonnet-2 141-144. The guard-wrap exception is not exercised. The only if is opus-1 line 206 `if currency =~ ~r/\A[A-Z]{3}\z/ do`, a block. The new Formatting bullet under "How to use this skill" is not a rule heading; it bears on this rule only through the wrapped-do: shape, which no file has. As before, one-expression bodies written as blocks are not counted.

Unchanged rule, graded to the previous sweep's standard: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function", decided by "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 152). Violating runs: 2 of 5 (previous sweep 1 of 5, haiku-2). Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 write the same three helpers as the previous sweep's haiku-2: parse_amount/1 and parse_placed_at/1 are one-step withs that nest a case in the body (sonnet-1 lines 113-114 and 123-124, sonnet-2 117-118 and 127-128), the rule's own "Instead of" example, and parse_status/1 calls the status clauses in the body (sonnet-1 132-133, sonnet-2 136-137). Their parse_order/1 withs have five steps (sonnet-1 87-91, sonnet-2 91-95). The other three chain every lookup and parse in one with: nine steps in opus-1 (163-171), eight in haiku-1 (84-91) and haiku-2 (71-78). All five write build/1's single parse call as a case with `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` (opus-1 line 65, haiku-1 63, haiku-2 53, sonnet-1 63, sonnet-2 67).

Unchanged rule, graded to the previous sweep's standard: "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job", decided by "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 225). Hand-written per-key fold: 0 of 5 (previous sweep 0 of 5). All five group by customer with Enum.group_by/2, then Map.new/2 (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) or Enum.map/2 into a sorted list (haiku-2 121-126). Per-currency totals use Enum.group_by/3 then Map.new/2 (opus-1 116-117, haiku-1 148-149, sonnet-2 167-168) or Enum.group_by/2 then Map.new/2 (haiku-2 144-145, sonnet-1 161-162). Completed orders are counted with Enum.frequencies_by/2 in opus-1 (129), haiku-1 (165) and sonnet-1 (175), Enum.count/2 per group in sonnet-2 (173), and length/1 of a filtered list that also feeds the totals in haiku-2 (137); all are held clean as before. The Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces, and the reduce_while loops build lists.

Naming, captures, the list, date, money, atom and process rules are unchanged and graded to the earlier standard; all five are clean on each. Naming per sentence, out of 5: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0 (every module is under Reports); boolean functions end in ? 0 (haiku-1's completed?/1 is the only boolean function); get/fetch 0 (every checking lookup is string_field/2); size/length 0; ignored values 0; domain variable names 0 (text, parsed, id, latest and other are held as before). Captures: haiku-2 and sonnet-1 sum with &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2), which the rule names as clean; opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2 use &Decimal.add/2; haiku-2's &{-&1.completed_count, &1.customer_id} (line 160) is held clean as in earlier grades; every fn destructures a tuple or wraps a case. Lists: opus-1 (line 76) and haiku-2 (line 65) prepend without reversing, held clean as the previous sweep's haiku-1 because nothing downstream depends on the order.

Other rules follow the earlier standard. Opus-1's @doc on the public Order.parse/1 (lines 153-160) has no ## Examples, listed under the Comments rule; its build/1 now has a doctest, and the other four document only build/1, each with a doctest. Sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's case inside a one-step with is also listed under Keep functions short, as the previous sweep listed haiku-2's. Sonnet-1's string_field/2 now has a `%{^key => _value} -> {:error, {:invalid_field, key}}` clause (line 107) before `%{} ->`, so the previous sweep's Match every expected shape finding does not recur; sonnet-2's is the same (line 111). reduce_while piped into case (sonnet-1 line 73, sonnet-2 line 77) is not listed, as before. The changed multi-line-argument rule ("Unless a call's result is bound to a name ...") is not broken: no call takes a map, struct or keyword literal spanning several lines; the multi-line maps are return values (opus-1 85-88, haiku-2 134-139, sonnet-2 149-152, 158-161) or bound to a name (the %Order{} in each parse_order). Every defstruct lists bare atoms or @enforce_keys, and alias lines sit right after @moduledoc.
